description: Structural ground truth for simple.md / simple.docx / simple.pdf / simple.html. The image fixtures (simple.png / simple.jpeg) carry only a subset -- see image_subset. All three encode identical content, so any per-format difference in extraction output is a property of the parser, not the fixture.
title: Quarterly Infrastructure Report
paragraphs: This report summarizes platform capacity, notable changes, and planned work for the third quarter. It is intended for the infrastructure team and their partners in product engineering.

Total cluster capacity grew by 18 percent this quarter, driven mainly by the expansion of the eu-central-1 region. Request volume grew faster, at 26 percent, so average utilization rose despite the added hardware.
No customer-visible outages were recorded. Two internal incidents were raised, both resolved within the same working day, and neither breached the error budget.
The figures below cover managed compute only. Object storage, the data warehouse, and third-party services are reported separately and are out of scope for this document.
The table below shows node counts and average utilization for the final week of the quarter. Utilization is measured as mean CPU allocation during business hours.
Three actions are proposed for the coming quarter, in priority order.
Questions and corrections should go to the platform team. A detailed cost breakdown is available on request.

items: Managed compute across all four production regions
Scheduled batch workloads running on shared nodes
Internal staging clusters, excluding developer sandboxes
Add twelve nodes to eu-central-1 before the end of month one.
Migrate batch workloads off ap-south-1 and consolidate them in us-west-2.
Review reserved failover capacity, which has not been exercised in three quarters.

metadata_title.comment: DOCX, PDF and HTML all carry the title in a metadata channel as well as in the body. Markdown has no metadata channel. Read it from the metadata, not the body, or the title will be counted twice.

render.source: reportlab PDF rasterized with pdftoppm, then autocropped
render.jpeg: quality 95, subsampling 0 (4:4:4), same pixel buffer as the PNG
render.replica: Same dimensions and same layout. Not pixel-identical -- JPEG is lossy: ~19% of pixels differ, max channel delta 9, mean 0.21.

ocr_baseline.png: exact match against expected_text after normalization

ocr_baseline.comment: Both images OCR cleanly at this tier, so a wrong result is the pipeline, not the fixture. Note that OCR returns text only -- recovering the 5x4 table shape needs layout analysis, so expect the tables column to be empty for these two rows unless the extractor does table detection on images.

notes.heading_depth: H1 title, three H2 sections, one H3 subsection.
notes.pdf_tables: Ruled with a full grid, so line-based detectors (pdfplumber) find it without strategy tuning.
notes.text_parity: Normalized prose (lowercased, punctuation and list markers stripped, table cells removed) is identical across all four files: 1534 characters each.
notes.html_semantics: Semantic tags only -- h1/h2/h3, p, ul, ol, table with thead/tbody. No CSS, no scripts, no nav or footer chrome, no wrapper div. Body cells are all <td>, matching the header-row-only shape of the other three.
notes.html_title_tripwire: A regex tag-stripper will pull <title> into the body text and report the title twice. Parse the DOM and read <body>, or take the title from metadata. This is deliberate -- it catches naive extraction paths.
notes.encoding: ASCII only, except the bullet glyph the DOCX/PDF renderers emit for unordered list items.
